title: The Long Climb in JGB Yields Is Nearly Over
standfirst: JGB yields saw a historic rise between 2022 and 2026. Most of the rise came from higher inflation expectations and a normalization of term premia. Our analysis shows the Long Climb is likely nearly over.
_note: Titles, source notes and y-axis labels are the TITLE / SOURCE / YLABEL constants of each chart script in the JMA chart library, copied verbatim. Windows, chart form and series labels are read off the same scripts' plotting code — the data CSV cannot carry them.

charts.section: Behind the article: the decomposition at each maturity
charts.section_note: The article argues the Long Climb was driven by two forces — the end of deflation lifting expected policy rates, and term premia normalising as the BoJ withdrew. These four charts show that split directly, at each long maturity. Reading down them, the balance shifts: at 10 years roughly three-quarters of the rise since January 2022 is expectations, while at 30 and 40 years the term premium accounts for about half. Same model, same vintage, as the yield-curve model page.
charts.title: At 10 years, the rise is mostly about expected policy rates
charts.subtitle: 10Y spot yield decomposed into expected policy rates and the term premium
charts.source: Source: JMA JGB yield-curve model, vintage 19 July 2026. Lightened bars and the dotted line from August 2026 = JMA baseline projection.
charts.note: Of the 2.55pp rise between January 2022 and July 2026, 1.89pp is higher expected policy rates and 0.66pp is a wider term premium. The term premium was slightly negative in January 2022 and is 0.64% now — still below its 1.34% high of July 2004.

charts.title: At 20 years, the term premium takes a larger share
charts.subtitle: 20Y spot yield decomposed into expected policy rates and the term premium
charts.source: Source: JMA JGB yield-curve model, vintage 19 July 2026. Lightened bars and the dotted line from August 2026 = JMA baseline projection.
charts.note: Of the 3.15pp rise since January 2022, 1.83pp is expectations and 1.31pp the term premium — 42% against 26% at the 10-year point.

charts.title: At 30 years, the term premium did just over half the work
charts.subtitle: 30Y spot yield decomposed into expected policy rates and the term premium
charts.source: Source: JMA JGB yield-curve model, vintage 19 July 2026. Lightened bars and the dotted line from August 2026 = JMA baseline projection.
charts.note: Of the 3.47pp rise since January 2022, 1.76pp is the term premium against 1.71pp from expectations. This is the tenor the article flags as still moderately elevated: the 30Y term premium is 2.07%, essentially at its 2.08% high of June 2026, and has not yet turned down the way the 40Y has.

charts.title: At 40 years, the two forces split the rise almost evenly
charts.subtitle: 40Y spot yield decomposed into expected policy rates and the term premium
charts.source: Source: JMA JGB yield-curve model, vintage 19 July 2026. Lightened bars and the dotted line from August 2026 = JMA baseline projection.
charts.note: Of the 3.26pp rise since January 2022, 1.65pp is expectations and 1.61pp the term premium. The series begins in November 2007, when the 40-year JGB was first issued. The 40Y term premium peaked at 2.24% in November 2025 and has eased to 1.88% — the turn the article points to as an early sign the long end has stopped rising.
